## Simple explanation

vLLM is software for running and serving large language models efficiently,
especially when many requests or long sequences must share GPU memory.

## Technical explanation

vLLM is an inference and serving framework whose techniques include
PagedAttention, continuous batching, and optimized kernels. Its memory
management allows key-value cache blocks to be allocated flexibly, helping
improve throughput under suitable workloads. Performance depends on hardware,
model architecture, sequence lengths, batch composition, and runtime settings.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Serving cost and latency can dominate production LLM systems. An inference
engine can improve utilization and expose APIs, but engineers still need to
measure request-level latency, throughput, memory use, quality, and failure
behavior on the actual deployment workload.

## How it works

The engine loads model weights, schedules incoming requests, batches token
generation steps, and manages per-request key-value state. Continuous
batching can admit or finish requests while other sequences continue decoding.

## Practical example

Serve a supported instruction model through vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API.
Benchmark representative prompt and output lengths under realistic concurrent
load, and compare tail latency and throughput rather than relying on a single
tokens-per-second number.

## Common misconceptions

- An inference engine does not improve the model's underlying correctness or
  safety by itself.
- A benchmark on one GPU or request mix does not predict production performance
  on another model, hardware, or concurrency level.
